In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the geochemical composition of varves as a proxy for the reconstruction of past environmental conditions in Lake Donguz- Orun.
the development of a new approach to the study of the geochemistry and paleoecology of varved sediments, and to the reconstruction of paleoclimatic and paleoecological conditions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the studied varves of Lake Donguz- Orun bottom sediments contain geochemical signals of seasonal variations in the composition of atmospheric precipitation and the lake water.
the geochemical data from the varved sediments of Lake Donguz- Orun are in agreement with the meteorological data and with the isotopic chronology.
the studied geochemical indicators are useful for the reconstruction of the history of the lake and its catchment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
synchrotron-based scanning X-ray fluorescence is an effective technique for the analysis of varve structure in bottom sediments.
synchrotron X-ray methods are a promising tool for studying the inner structure of varves and for identifying geochemical signals in sediments of lakes with a long-term record of climate change.
